findings.observation: Kernel standing is never checked. Claim comparison filters "row.Standing == KernelStanding.Owned" (:290); the kernel set is a literal in the test (:221 ["Events.IDomainEvent", "IEntity", "IConcurrencyTokenEntity"]) not tied to the Kernel rows. Changing the row to CatalogueRow.Kernel("Delivery"), or adding a fourth Kernel row, skips every blocker check and the type is not a free mover, so the suite stays green. No planted falsifier for a false Kernel claim.
findings.remediation: Add a check that rows with Standing Kernel equal exactly the allowed kernel types (both ways, naming type and fix), one declared list shared by catalogue and measurement, plus a made-up-world case where a Kernel row is claimed for a non-kernel type and fails naming it.
